items.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: it’s like the whole Monica Lewinsky thing. You know? Are you really that interested in that that you’re going to spend all that — think of the money which has been generated between advertising, newspeople’s salaries and camera crews and microwave transmitters.

ctx.x: The jazz scene taken as a total, you’ve got some white racists and you’ve got some black racists. So it all adds up to zero, right? It’s like the expanding universe you know. It all adds up to zero. There’s as much going out that way as there is going this way, you add them up, they cancel out. But no, in all seriousness, jazz and the jazz viewpoint, the jazz perspective, is the one perspective, historically speaking now, from the early part of the century on up to now, that I’ve seen, has been the one area where…
